how: A member starts by proposing shared representation and gives others a canvas project to join.
Repeated appeals recruit people for representation, a wordmark, and renewed figure work.
Participants assess limited hands, crowding, and likely conflict when deciding what they can attempt.
Participants choose between figures and lettering, simplify proposals, and revise the mark around nearby art.
Individual pixels and letters become public progress reports and a reported completed wordmark.
Asking for a starting point and a template supplies the instruction-seeking minimum without establishing a settled shared template.
A repairer answers the attack announcement with a brief commitment to fixing the figure.
Participants guard the completed wordmark, request relief, repair letters, and answer attack warnings.
An apparent overwriter explains an unrefreshed view and receives thanks, distinguishing mistaken interference from intended damage.
Participants appeal to prior occupancy, refuse intrusion, apologize for damage, and request preservation of neighbouring work.
Damage complaints and space requests prompt agreement proposals and discussion of accommodating neighbouring figures.
Participants request support, offer restoration and shared-space help, and thank outside helpers.
A visitor carries another group's space request and a project participant relays the issue to workers and chat.
Permission-seeking fits the candidate's request-side minimum without demonstrating that a host approved or ruled over the work.
A request for permission establishes neither host consent nor continuing dependence on a host's rule.
One member proposes destroying occupied art and continues through a collision while promising compensation elsewhere.
Repeated hostile kiwi phrases carry the border conflict in talk without proving coordinated destructive placements.
Reported destruction prompts looking for another place and asking wordmark builders where a figure could be rebuilt.
Participants celebrate completion, credit helpers, and recount their contributions alongside continuing repair.
Participants report the damaged ending, memorialize Apollo, and describe the half-head left when placement closed.
Fake announcements, character jokes and a takeover coexist with explicit evaluation of April Fools creativity.
Familiar franchise lore supplies a joke for interpreting Apollo's damaged ending.
A moderator redirects a duplicate toward a more active coordination thread while another participant asks for a sticky.
A negotiated guard handoff is visible, so lack of formal leadership cannot imply no decided allocation of work.
The destruction proposal invokes crowded space rather than identifying a quarrel carried into the canvas.
A space-based destruction proposal and a later franchise joke cannot establish a pre-existing tie causing an attack.
Suspected opposing scripts do not establish that participants adopted bots, scripts or spare accounts themselves.
Offers of help and completion support do not establish coalition membership or a mutual-defense organization.
Post-close thanks and memorial language do not show a decision to continue the collective or remake the work elsewhere.
Hostile replies to preservation requests do not dispute who may speak for or bind the room.
Mourning the damaged final figure does not show contest over a cleaned copy or an authoritative historical account.
The public wordmark call receives explicit reports of joining that project and completing a letter.
A proposal and recruitment can occur in the same turn rather than forming separate successive stages.
The standing edit explicitly makes holding the fort the next task after reported completion, although its edit time is unavailable.
Crowded construction can prompt border accommodation before a completed mark needs maintenance.
Prior occupancy can justify restraint without a settled border, while agreement remains proposed and other participants continue hostile replies.
Public repairs and suspicion of opposing scripts cannot test whether upkeep caused own-side automation inside partly unseen coordination.
A report of finishing the Ace portion immediately celebrates that completed part.
Later speakers explicitly connect fate reports to attack and closure, so earlier celebration alone does not establish the recording mechanism.
Reports and mourning reveal no subsequent decision about carrying the effort forward.
Judged shortage can produce postponement or concession rather than a move, while separately reported destruction prompts relocation.
Template questions demonstrate demand for instructions but do not show a posted template settling the design dispute.
Joining can explain fatigue with another ruined project or request instructions, while a bare repair acceptance remains locally visible.
The suggestion to seek outside support directly answers interference with the wordmark's letters.
A later outside offer in another branch does not establish that the public support suggestion caused the helper's arrival.
A relocation request opens an explicit sharing proposal and subsequent promise to help complete the figure.
Destructive proposals occur during recruitment, but participants cite collision and scarce space rather than the call itself as their reason.
Restraint can receive renewed hostility instead of following an attack call, and the speakers do not form a shared position.
Separated destruction proposals and agreement talk do not demonstrate that an attack call caused negotiation.
A hostile kiwi refrain answers the war-call branch, sustaining the contest as talk without verifying a raid.
Defense and individual help do not show maintenance producing coalition membership.
A duplicate-thread redirect and sticky request show concentrating coordination without establishing a flood-driven containment response.
Agreement proposals and hostile preservation replies do not test whether negotiated commitments prompted disputes over representative authority.
Precautionary redesign reduces a figure's overlap and anticipated retaliation before erasure requires relocation.
Invitations and relayed neighbour issues move coordination through chat while leaving its internal decisions outside the public record.

how: A participant carries a neighbour's space issue to workers and Discord, connecting public border negotiation with backstage coordination.
A request to preserve neighbouring work receives a hostile refrain and its echo, carrying restraint talk into renewed contention.
A surviving expansion title warrants only an announcement, not an explanation of the canvas or verification that expansion occurred.
